title: AI-Run Modern LaTeX Manuscript Workflow and Replication Packet
description:
Compact workflow and replication record for the Modern LaTeX Editions of Mathematics Manuscripts project. It documents the AI-run scan-to-TeX-to-translation-to-audit-to-publication workflow, including local source acquisition, OCR/math-OCR witness generation, source-image slicing, high-DPI object crops, TeX compilation, web review handoffs, GitHub mirroring, and Zenodo publication.

Latest update, 2026-06-25. Adds source-witness/public-surface and archive-scope guardrail addenda from current SGA, Noether, Gordan, Steinitz, Deligne, Cayley, and local sweep maintenance lessons, plus a failed-web salvage rule from Noether repair work. This update also adds the SGA5 and Weber find-verify-fix method snapshots. The SGA5 snapshot packages page-local discovery, independent source verification, deterministic old-string/new-string patching, compile gates, and the lesson that agent/swarm passes are finders rather than certifiers. The Weber snapshot adapts the same method to German transcription/source-completeness first: detect omissions, compression, and missing formulae before English translation; no native >=650 dpi Weber scan is currently on disk, with Band I/III around 500 dpi and Band II around 560 dpi, so hard symbols require tight crops and explicit uncertainty flags. The GitHub mirror now carries the Weber method/certification logs through Band I p155. The refreshed packet includes the current Weber certification and method logs through Band I p155: p100/p102 received determinant/proof/formula repairs; p106 restored a dropped theorem numeral; p108-p143 restored sign-schema/equation/tag/figure, roots-of-unity, variable, dense-proof, Newton-footnote, and symmetric-function material; p144-p155 add small omission repairs, tuple restoration, the p154 beta-gamma sign repair, and rejected false candidates at p147/p155. Current Weber method cursor: p156-p161 next.

The addenda formalize the difference between OCR/source-witness aids, failed-run locator packets, working drafts, source-witnessed tranches, source-closed loci, critical editions, and unrelated local mathematical files that should not be published as part of this project.

Scope guardrail. Local sweep may inspect broad folders, but publication is limited to the manuscript transcription/translation/source-audit project unless Floris explicitly requests a named non-project upload. A file being mathematical, interesting, recently downloaded, or technically publishable is not enough.

Workflow status. The record is a reusable workflow packet, not a claim that any particular mathematical edition is critically complete. OCR, VLM, detector, crop, candidate-TeX, derivative PDF, failed web-run transcript, and source-inventory outputs are witness and locator layers unless a source-specific audit promotes them. Source scans and source-object witnesses remain authority for transcription claims.

Corrections and contributions. Workflow corrections, tool notes, reproducibility improvements, and issue reports can be suggested through the GitHub mirror via issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
version: 2026-06-25 source-witness, archive-scope, failed-web salvage, and SGA5/Weber method snapshots
notes: Adds workflow_addendum_20260624_source_witness_public_surface.md, workflow_addendum_20260624_archive_scope_guardrail.md, the compact archive-scope guardrail ZIP, the 2026-06-25 failed-web salvage rule now documented in docs/workflow.md, AI_Run_Workflow_SGA5_FindVerifyFix_Workpass_Method_20260625.zip (149526 bytes, SHA256 7808CC08461D9274A2FA280644ABBDEF0DA09DF67ADD7B8940C642D9747BE88F), and AI_Run_Workflow_Weber_FindVerifyFix_Audit_Method_20260625.zip (45807 bytes, SHA256 B7259670AA4FB6CCF4DDE1C71DC4C56CBAC7A2B7FFD09DA82F0CFB45B3ABFEA4). Core rules: do not let filenames carry quality claims; OCR is a coverage/source locator, not authority; high-resolution source packets should include page maps, object inventories, crops with context, output renders, stable object IDs, and ledger verdicts; failed or crashed web-review runs may be preserved as salvage/locator evidence only when they carry explicit do-not-promote/no-fix-trap ledgers and source-quality notes; SGA5/Weber-style agents and OCR/witness workflows are finders/check layers, not certification by themselves; audit bundles should be routed as provenance/support unless they close a public-facing uncertainty; found-on-disk does not mean publish; unrelated third-party TeX, new research drafts, Reddit downloads, Lean experiments, and personal/novel math files stay out unless Floris explicitly names the exact item for upload; critical-edition language is reserved for explicit human certification.
